div.head: VI Atr Lat 40.2
div.ab: K. Haec itaque legalia statuta uel decreta, in nostro conuentu sinodali a rege N. (Æþelredo) magnopere edicta, cuncti tunc temporis optimates se obseruaturos fideliter spondebant; idcircoque ego N. (Þulfstanus), gratia Domini disponente Eboracensium archiepiscopus, eadem ad sequentium memoriam, necnon et ad praesentium uel futurorum salutem, litteris infixi, Domini uidelicet proximique dilectione conpunctus.

[Trans. Wormald, Making] And so these legal statutes or decrees were urgently issued at our synodical assembly by king N. All the magnates at that time promised they would obey them faithfully. And for that reason, I N., archbishop of York by disposition of the grace of the Lord, driven of course by the love of the Lord and of neighbour, committed the same to writing for the memory of posterity and the salvation of present and future.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)
